title: Enhancing Collective Communication in MCM Accelerators for Deep Learning Training
problem: Current MCM accelerator approaches fail to fully utilize available links in mesh interconnection networks, resulting in suboptimal AllReduce performance for distributed deep learning training. Mesh topologies are underutilized because existing algorithms do not leverage bidirectional interconnects effectively.
motivation: As deep learning models scale to massive sizes, multi-chip-module accelerators require efficient collective communication algorithms to enable practical distributed training across multiple chips.
method: Two algorithms improve AllReduce performance in mesh-based accelerators (systems of multiple chips connected via grid-like networks). RingBiOdd takes advantage of bidirectional links by creating two separate one-way rings, allowing both transmission directions to operate simultaneously and doubling throughput. Three Tree Overlap (TTO) builds three separate tree-shaped paths through the mesh (each optimized for the network's structure) and overlaps different computation stages across these trees, enabling parallel execution instead of sequential processing.
key_novelty: Overlapping AllReduce computation stages across multiple separate tree paths (each shaped to the mesh structure) so more network links transmit simultaneously.
contributions: RingBiOdd algorithm that creates dual unidirectional rings from bidirectional mesh interconnects
Three Tree Overlap (TTO) algorithm with topology-aware disjoint trees and parallel step execution
Detailed design and implementation of both collective communication algorithms
Experimental validation on seven DL models showing 33-50% training time reduction over baselines

metrics.speedup: 50% vs Ring, 33% vs MultiTree, 29% vs Bidirectional Ring

limitations: Scalability to other network topologies and applicability to non-reduction collective operations not discussed.
primary_theme: Optimizing collective communication for mesh-based MCM accelerators
